summary: Chrome extension (Interlude timer + reminder library) whose change is real engineering: a pure validation/command model (extension/model.js) with optimistic expectedRevision concurrency, full saved-reminder CRUD, and a worker that persists accepted data before reconciling alarms/windows and warns when the after-effect fails. 39 Node + 10 Chromium tests all present on disk and matching the evidence logs exactly. Off-stack: no HTTP, SQL, React or auth in delivered code.

summary: Not a SQL course despite the name: IPSKILL is a React 19 + TypeScript app that displays a six-track lesson archive. Astra replaced a silent localStorage autosave with an IndexedDB commit that does read-compare-write in one transaction and rejects on {id, revision} mismatch, added shared runtime contracts so the import path cannot bypass form validation, versioned practice-project CRUD with an injectable clock, and real search/filter/pagination. 69 checks, every sub-count reconcilable on disk, with two mid-verification failures disclosed. Scope is really a rewrite (App.tsx 308 to 1,098 lines, seven new modules) and there is no server, SQL or auth.

name: buildwhiteboard

summary: Best CRUD-web code in the batch. The original server would not boot (CommonJS require inside a type:module package); Astra rebuilt it as a testable factory with a real HTTP metadata API: 201 + Location on create vs 200 on open, 409 on stale version, 404 for tombstoned IDs that can never be recreated, plus 400/413/415. store.js persists via temp-file + rename BEFORE mutating live Yjs state or broadcasting, with a test that forces a real rename failure and proves server, peer and disk bytes all unchanged. 17 backend + 8 browser tests, exact match. Cost: extremely dense single-line JSX and heavy CRDT vocabulary in only 4,419 words.

name: formforge
top_fix: Add an 'if this fails, it means' table to astraupskill/README.md mapping the four documented environment failures (offline install gap, Turbo ancestor-directory permission error, 5s API test timeout on a cold parallel run, blocked PowerShell shim) to their fixes.
summary: Four genuine bugs found by reasoning, each with a regression test written first: a public slug any workspace could take over (now 409 slug_unavailable), a publication ID built from a per-slug counter that produced duplicate IDs colliding with submission idempotency keys (now per-form index + UUID), routes storing a body naming a different form than the URL (now 400 form_identity_mismatch), and an autosave whose stale in-flight response reported 'Saved' while a newer edit was still debouncing. 82 tests reconcile exactly including the it.each expansion; there is a runnable labs/publication-trace.ts. Also the most honest: loadWorkspace is a fixture behind useQuery, storage is in-memory, x-workspace-id is a spoofable header - all stated up front. No database anywhere.

name: geminiorganized/LLM_Generated_Helper
top_fix: Separate the two applications: move the journal to its own folder and package.json, and restore the root README/package.json description to the AI Call Assistant, which Astra demoted to 'legacy' in its own manifest.
summary: Host project is an off-target Electron AI assistant, so Astra wrote a new dependency-free CRUD app inside it: a loopback Practice Journal over profiles/questions/sessions/attempts with bearer auth, revision + writer-lease optimistic concurrency, server-side search and pagination, lifecycle rules, referential integrity and immutable question snapshots, plus a rigorous HTTP envelope (Host/Origin/sec-fetch-site, 405/413/415/422, CSP). Second lesson from the host app: the original settings store mutated its cache before the write succeeded and silently erased undecryptable credentials; both fixed with a regression asserting memory and disk unchanged after an injected rename failure. 120 Node tests exactly countable on disk plus 14 named browser and 6 mocked renderer checks. Costs: zero TypeScript/React/framework/SQL, and the delivery repositioned the host project around the new app.
